Maya K: Heads up — product asked if we can surface an SLA card in the console that shows per-tenant SLO variance and a button to open "variance inspector".
Samir: do you mean a tile on the route detail page? :thinking_face:
Maya K: yep, on the route page and on the tenant overview. Needs to show current window vs target, last breach timestamp, and a quick link to alert rules.
Devon: big Q — should the card drive routing policy changes (auto quiet / downgrade) or just be informational?
Liam: prefer informational first. automated routing from UI feels risky. maybe an opt-in rollout flag.
Nora: agree. If we expose an "auto-mitigate" toggle we need strong audit + confirm step and an approval flow.
Maya K: UX ask: highlight noisy rules and offer debounce suggestions. e.g., "rule X fires 12x/day — suggest 10m debounce"
Samir: for debounce suggestions we need telemetry query + histogram of inter-alert deltas. I can add a lightweight endpoint: `/api/v1/alerts/intervals?route_id=...`
Devon: sample output:
```
{ "route_id": "route-123", "p50_interval_s": 360, "p90_interval_s": 600, "count_24h": 45 }
```
Maya K: nice. On the card we can show a recommended debounce and a confidence level.
Liam: routing policy conflict: tenant-level quiet windows vs route-level debounce — which wins?
Nora: precedence: tenant-level > route-level. That matches how we do quota overrides today.
Samir: note: implementing suggested debounce requires we synthesize a preview of expected noise reduction. That's compute-heavy if we run full sim, but we can do an estimate based on intervals and current alert rate.
Devon: also need guardrails for multi-tenant routes. If tenant A toggles auto-mitigate it should not affect tenant B.
Maya K: rollout plan: feature flag (console.sla_card_inspector) -> internal beta -> gradual opt-in per org -> GA.
ops-bot: deploy succeeded for feature/console-sla-card on staging (build: bb7a9) :white_check_mark:
Samir: I'll sketch the API and prototype telemetry query today. tagging @Liam for precedence rules and @Nora for audit requirements.
Liam: I'll write a short RFC for policy precedence and bake in an audit events schema (`event_type: policy_change`, `actor`, `reason`).
Nora: +1 on events schema. Also require a human confirmation for any auto-mitigate rollout > 1k qps.
Maya K: perfect. next step: Samir + Devon to prototype the inspector data shape; Liam + Nora draft the precedence + audit; I'll mock the UI card.
Samir: starting now, will drop a WIP link in #eng-platform when ready.
